rotation_note: good to a few tenths of a degree: a two-view essential matrix is weakly conditioned when the baseline is small next to the scene depth. The verdict uses the displacement, not this
translation_note: direction only, in the reference camera frame; two views cannot give its length without a known length in the scene
homography_note: a high fraction means one plane, or a near-pure rotation, explains the matches; the rotation stays usable but the translation direction does not
verdict: the camera has moved: matched scene points are a median 55 px apart, of the order of 2.2 degrees of rotation, against a 3 px limit. The extrinsic, the table plane and the sim-camera export all have to be redone
what_to_redo: run_rgbcal.sh lock (a new setup session for the current viewpoint)
run_realsim.sh scale-check, until the error is inside the tolerance
caveats: feature matching counts everything that moved, including people, chairs and the blocks; a low inlier fraction means the scene changed a lot, not that the camera did not move
